blocks.task_summary: Find the total number of possible three-digit codes abc using digits {1,2,3,4,5} with no repetition.
Given P(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+c has factor (x^2+3x+2) with a,b,c distinct from {1,2,3,4,5}, find b in terms of a.
method_path: apply factor theorem: P(-1)=0 and P(-2)=0
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Let P(x)=(x^2+3x+2)(x+d), expand to x^3+(d+3)x^2+(3d+2)x+2d, compare coefficients: a=d+3 and b=3d+2, eliminate d to get b=3a-7
METHOD 3: Divide x^3+ax^2+bx+c by x^2+3x+2, set remainder 3a-b-7=0
METHOD 4: Factor x^2+3x+2=(x+1)(x+2), use Vieta with roots -1,-2,p to get b=3a-7

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (x^2+3x+2)=(x+1)(x+2) A1, factor theorem M1, attempt two equations M1, equations A1, eliminate c M1, b=3a-7 A1
METHOD 2: P(x)=(x^2+3x+2)(x+d) M1, expansion A1, compare coefficients M1, a=d+3 and b=3d+2 A1, eliminate d M1, b=3a-7 A1
METHOD 3: division M1, quotient x+a-3 A1, remainder (3a-b-7)x A1, set to zero M1, b=3a-7 A1
METHOD 4: Vieta A1, roots -1,-2,p M1, sum a-3=p A1, product pairs b=... A1, eliminate p M1, b=3a-7 A1

blocks.task_summary: Show that the only assignment satisfying all conditions is a=4, b=5, c=2.
method_path: use b=3a-7 and c from P(-1)=0 or c=2a-6
test a=1,2,5: b outside {1,...,5} or repeats a
a=3 gives b=2, c=0 (0 not allowed)
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: use c=2a-6, argue a=4 is the only possibility from the digit set {1,2,3,4,5}

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: a=1,2,5 lead to invalid values for b R1; a=3 gives b=2, c=0 so not possible R1; so a=4,b=5,c=2 AG
METHOD 2: c=2a-6 R1; correctly argues a=4 is the only possibility R1; so a=4,b=5,c=2 AG

blocks.task_summary: Express P(x)=x^3+4x^2+5x+2 as a product of linear factors.
Sketch y=P(x)=x^3+4x^2+5x+2 showing intercepts with axes.
method_path: positive cubic shape with y-intercept at (0,2)
local maximum point between x=-2 and x=-1
accepted_alternatives: calculus approach using f'(x) to find turning points

evidence.basis: positive cubic shape with y-intercept at (0,2) A1; x-intercept at (-2,0) and local maximum point anywhere between x=-2 and x=-1 A1; local minimum point at (-1,0) A1. Note: Accept answers from an approach based on calculus.
